sections.h2: What does the Randolph County Register of Deeds do when you sell a house?
sections.html:
It is the office where your deed to the buyer is recorded and becomes part of the public land record for Randolph County. It also records deeds of trust, powers of attorney, releases, plats, condominium maps and related papers, and it cancels paid-off deeds of trust by recording a certificate of satisfaction.

The same office issues marriage licenses, keeps certified copies of births, deaths and marriages that happened in the county, and swears in notaries. For a seller, the real estate side is what matters. A sale does not bind a buyer's lender or later purchasers against other claimants until the deed is on record, a rule found in G.S. 47-18.

The register of deeds is an elected county office, chosen by the county's voters every two years under G.S. 161-1.

sections.h2: When is the Randolph County Register of Deeds open, and when must a deed arrive?
sections.html:
The office is open 8 am to 5 pm, Monday through Friday, but real estate recording stops earlier. The county commissioners authorized the office by resolution to suspend recording of real estate documents, notary oaths and marriage licenses at 4:30 pm every day.

That half hour matters on closing day. If your closing attorney sends a deed over late in the afternoon, plan for it to be accepted before 4:30 or to wait for the next business day. The office follows the same holiday closings as the rest of Randolph County government, and the county posts a yearly list.

sections.h2: Where is the Randolph County Register of Deeds office in Asheboro?
sections.html:
It sits in the Shaw Building in Asheboro. The county's directions from Highway 64 say to turn north onto Cox Street, follow it to Worth Street and turn left at the light, and the building is on the left.

Coming from the Highway 220 bypass, take the Asheboro (Highway 42) exit, turn east onto Salisbury Street, turn right at the light where it meets North Fayetteville Street, then take the left-turn lane onto Worth Street. From that direction the Shaw Building is on the right.

If you cannot visit, the office will still answer questions by email through its county page. Wills are not kept here. They go to the Randolph County Clerk of Court, who also holds older books with a page reference ending in the letter E.

sections.h2: What does the Randolph County Register of Deeds charge to record a deed?
sections.html:
Fees follow the uniform state schedule in G.S. 161-10, and counties cannot add their own. An ordinary instrument costs $26.00 for up to 15 pages and $4.00 for each page past that. A deed of trust or mortgage costs $64.00 for up to 35 pages, plus the same $4.00 per extra page.

  • Recording a satisfaction or cancellation of a deed of trust carries no fee.
  • A plat is $21.00 per sheet.
  • A certified copy is $5.00 for the first page and $2.00 for each added page.
  • A nonstandard document adds $25.00, and each extra instrument within one filing adds $10.00.

The statute calls these fees complete and exclusive, and they are collected before the document is filed. Ask the office which payment forms it takes.

sections.h2: Who pays the North Carolina excise tax when a Randolph County home sells?
sections.html:
The seller does. Under G.S. 105-228.30 the transferor pays the tax to the register of deeds of the county where the land lies before the instrument is recorded. The rate is one dollar for each five hundred dollars of consideration or value, with any part of $500 counted as a full unit.

Half of the receipts stay with the county general fund and half go to the state, which is why the tax line is paid through this office rather than to the Department of Revenue directly. When a parcel straddles two counties, the county holding the greater value collects it. Your closing attorney normally figures the amount and brings the check.

sections.h2: How can you find or fix a recorded deed in Randolph County?
sections.html:
Search the county's online real estate records by name, book and page, subdivision or date range, and narrow by document type. You can also search the county GIS map by street address and follow the deed link for a copy.

  • Real estate index data and images run from January 1, 1986 to the present, with historical books 1071 through 1172 also available.
  • The plat index and images run from Book 1 to the present.
  • Names between 1986 and 1993 may appear abbreviated, such as Wm for William, so use Advanced Search with the match type set to contains.
  • Indexing has followed the state's minimum standards since January 1, 1994.

The office does not supply deed forms and does not give legal advice. To add or remove a name, a new deed has to be prepared and recorded, which means hiring an attorney or drafting it yourself.

sections.h2: Which other papers get recorded in a Randolph County sale?
sections.html:
Several instruments other than the deed can matter. G.S. 47-18 says a contract to convey, an option, a lease longer than three years and a right of first refusal or first offer do not protect anyone against lien creditors or purchasers for value until they are registered. Priority runs by the time of registration.

  • Seller-financed deals under Chapter 47H must be recorded, or a memorandum of the contract recorded, within five business days.
  • A buyer's lender files a deed of trust, and your old one is cleared by a recorded satisfaction.
  • Survey plats, condominium maps and assumed business names are filed in the same office.

Ask your closing attorney for a list of everything that will be filed so that nothing arrives after the 4:30 cutoff.

sections.h2: How do probate and unpaid property tax connect to the Randolph County office?
sections.html:
Probate is handled by the Randolph County Clerk of Court, and the register of deeds only records the deeds that follow. A small estate can use an affidavit when personal property less liens is no more than $20,000, usually after 30 days from the date of death, and the affidavit describes each tract of real estate the decedent owned.

Property tax is a separate track. The lien for a year's tax attaches on the date the property is to be listed, and the county can enforce it by a foreclosure action that resembles a mortgage foreclosure. A tax sale is a public auction at the courthouse door, and a higher bid may be filed within 10 days after the report of sale.

If you inherited the house or owe back taxes, ask the Randolph County tax office for a payoff figure before the deed is drafted.

sections.h2: What should a Randolph County seller check before closing day?
sections.html:
Confirm that your mortgage payoff will produce a recorded certificate of satisfaction, and then look the cancellation up in the online index afterward. The county's own answer to homeowners who ask where their deed went is that no one holds it except the owner or the attorney who handled the purchase.

Mobile homes are the other trap. Titles for them go through the state motor vehicle office, not through the register of deeds, so a buyer who is purchasing a mobile home on its own will need a different transfer path than a land deed. Ask the county tax office about listing and tax bills for the year of sale.

Whatever kind of buyer you have, the recording step is the same. Your closing attorney sends the signed, notarized deed here, and the office returns the recorded original to the address on the filing.

faqs.q: What time does Randolph County stop recording deeds?
faqs.a: Recording of real estate documents stops at 4:30 pm each day. The office itself stays open until 5 pm Monday through Friday, but a deed presented after the cutoff should be expected to wait.

faqs.q: Does the Randolph County Register of Deeds provide deed forms?
faqs.a: No. The only forms the office supplies are for assumed business names. For a deed you need an attorney, or you prepare it yourself, and the staff cannot advise you on wording.

faqs.q: Where do I file a will in Randolph County?
faqs.a: Wills go to the Randolph County Clerk of Court, not the register of deeds. The register's FAQ page lists the clerk's phone number for questions.

faqs.q: How do I get a copy of my recorded deed in Randolph County?
faqs.a: Search the register of deeds website by name or use the county GIS map by address and click the deed link. Book and page numbers ending in E mean the record sits with the Clerk of Court.

faqs.q: Is the deed excise tax paid by the buyer or the seller?
faqs.a: The seller pays it, to the register of deeds before recording. The rate is $1.00 per $500 of value or fractional part, and your closing attorney usually handles the payment.
